# Convert declination string to numeric degrees for comparison
def declination_to_degrees(dec_str):
    # Handle the format like " degree22′44″" or " degree20′53″"
    # Remove any leading/trailing whitespace
    dec_str = str(dec_str).strip()
    
    # Extract numbers using string operations
    # Find all numbers in the string (degrees, minutes, seconds)
    import re
    numbers = re.findall(r'[-+]?\d*\.?\d+', dec_str)
    
    if len(numbers) >= 1:
        degrees = float(numbers[0])
        minutes = float(numbers[1]) if len(numbers) > 1 else 0.0
        seconds = float(numbers[2]) if len(numbers) > 2 else 0.0
        return degrees + minutes/60 + seconds/3600
    else:
        return 0.0

spiral_df['declination_numeric'] = spiral_df['declination ( j2000 )'].apply(declination_to_degrees)
